name: Park Tax

established.purpose: Voter-approved parcel tax for parks, trees and landscaping maintenance (Measure F 1997; raised 2000, 2008, 2014 and by Measure Y in 2024)

legal_basis: Special parcel tax (two-thirds vote); rate $0.2652 per square foot of improvements after Measure Y (Nov 2024), indexed annually

annual.note: Combining Statement of Revenues, Expenditures and Changes in Fund Balances, Nonmajor Governmental Funds, ACFR p.243. Beginning balance 10,539,343

flows.instrument: Measure Y (November 2024, 75% yes); Council intent resolution Sept 24, 2024, Item 10
flows.stated_reason: Raise the Parks Tax from $0.221 to $0.2652 per square foot, about $3.8M a year, for park and landscape maintenance in the Waterfront including Cesar Chavez Park, the urban forest and park capital
flows.note: The ballot question named parks, trees and landscaping generally; the Council's pre-election resolution named the Waterfront.

flows.stated_reason: Waterfront park and landscape maintenance moved from the Marina Fund to the Parks Tax
flows.note: Staff: this shift alone covered the Marina Fund's $1.1M structural deficit. In FY2027-28 a further 5% of the Waterfront Deputy Director is shifted to the Parks Tax.

flows.to_fund: First Source Fund and Public Art Fund
flows.instrument: ACFR FY2025 combining statement; FY2026 AAO lists $26,925 and $68,119

obligations.note: Parks and camps unfunded need in the proposed FY2027-31 CIP; Measure Y contributes about $2.75M a year of park capital

status.years_in_deficit: Surplus in FY2024 and FY2025; balance rising
open_questions: How much of the Measure Y uplift is consumed by the Marina cost shift and the Deputy Director shift versus new park maintenance capacity.
Whether park maintenance staffing rose after Measure Y (FY2026 budget by program).
